capabilities.target: Customer account record, lookup by email or account id, not restricted to requester's own account

instructions.note: Agent may look up any customer by email or account id, with no instruction binding the lookup target to the requester's own identity, enabling confused-deputy data access.
The only stated control against cross-customer disclosure is a single prompt sentence, which is behavioral and decays with model capability.

Escalation to a human is keyed to customer sentiment ('angry') rather than to the sensitivity of the capability invoked, so a calm attacker's request for cross-account data is treated as routine and sent without review.

elements.name: Email recipient (arbitrary address reachable via shared mail credential)

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Behavioral instruction enforced only through model compliance; a more capable or longer-horizon model rationalizes exceptions or splits the disclosure across steps. Fails under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, autonomy_increase, and intended_purpose_change per control_decay.md.

controls.name: Human approval gate on outbound email carrying confidential data (recommended)
Recipient allowlist bound to ticket sender for outbound email (recommended)
Rate/spend/step limits on CRM reads and email sends (recommended)
Attributable audit logging of CRM read actions (recommended)

findings.title: Lethal trifecta / confused deputy (TC1, TC4): untrusted ticket content directs lookup and disclosure of another customer's record

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled ticket content specifies a target email or account id to look up (prompt.md:2-3 permits lookup by any identifier).
Agent calls get_customer with the attacker-supplied identifier; CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record (runtime notes), so the lookup is not bound to the requester's own account.

Agent sends the retrieved record back via mail_mcp.send; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address (runtime notes), and prompt.md:5-6 allows sending without human review unless the customer appears angry.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model.swappable is already true with no separate review per runtime notes ('the model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review'); any model/version change, a rise in unattended steps, or removal of the sentiment-based escalation check should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: "look up their account with get_customer. You may look up any customer by email or account id." No restriction binds the lookup target to the requester's own identity.
"If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry." Sends occur without approval regardless of data sensitivity.
"Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you." This is the only stated control against the exact path described above.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are reached with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN) rather than per-user delegated credentials.
"CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record" and "MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account. It can send to any address." confirm broad, not least-privilege, credential scope.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM lookups to the authenticated identity of the requesting customer (verify the sender address matches the account on file) instead of allowing lookup by any attacker-supplied email or account id.
Add a raw-action human approval gate for outbound emails carrying confidential CRM data, especially when the recipient does not match the original ticket sender.
Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN to least privilege / per-request credentials instead of broad read-all and send-to-any-address service accounts.
Restrict mail_mcp send to an allowlist bound to the original ticket's verified sender address (recipient confirmation bound to the system of record).

findings.title: Missing attributable audit trail for CRM reads and missing rate/step/spend limits on ticket processing

forecast.watch_signal: Rising ticket volume without added rate/step limits, or removal/weakening of SIEM logging for outbound email, indicates the gap is becoming exploitable at scale.

evidence.observation: "Every outbound email is logged to the SIEM." covers sends but no equivalent statement exists for CRM read actions, leaving reads unattributed.
No max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes is declared anywhere in the artifacts, and no spend/rate limit is mentioned for either crm_mcp or mail_mcp.

recommendations.action: Add per-agent and per-token rate/spend/step limits on CRM reads and outbound sends to bound resource consumption and mass data exfiltration attempts.
Log CRM read actions with the same attributable detail as outbound email, tying each read to the triggering ticket and customer claim for audit purposes.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how support-triage authenticates itself to the orchestration platform or MCP servers beyond possessing the bearer tokens in mcp.json; whether another process could impersonate this agent is not stated.
No information on how prompt.md or the agent's runtime configuration is protected against unauthorized modification in the deployment pipeline.
peer_identity_verified is false/unstated for crm_mcp; artifacts do not describe independent verification of the server's identity beyond the URL and bearer token.
definitions_pinned is not confirmed for crm_mcp's tool schema, so whether get_customer's definition could change after approval is unknown.
peer_identity_verified is not confirmed for mail_mcp beyond URL and bearer token possession.
definitions_pinned is not confirmed for mail_mcp's send tool schema.
This inbound flow carries attacker-authored content into the agent; it does not itself expose internal data outward. Outward disclosure is assessed on el.email_send_flow.
Artifacts do not state whether inbound ticket volume is throttled or rate-limited before reaching the agent.
mail_mcp is reached over HTTPS per mcp.json; in-transit tampering is addressed at the transport layer and is not a distinguishing design risk here.
Artifacts do not state whether inbound email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) or ticketing identity binding is used to attribute the request to a real sender.
The recipient is a passive message destination outside the agent's trust domain as modeled here, not an actor whose own actions this assessment must attribute.
Artifacts state emails are logged to the SIEM but do not describe integrity protections (write-once storage, hashing) against log tampering.
Whether the SIEM log retains full message bodies (including any confidential CRM data sent) and who can access it is not described.
SIEM ingestion capacity and retention are outside this agent's control surface; no capability of the agent can exhaust it beyond the email volume already assessed on el.email_send_flow.

rating.rationale: The agent lets an untrusted inbound email select any customer's account for lookup (no binding to the requester's own identity) and then send the result externally through a shared, broad-scope mail credential with no human approval gate and no recipient restriction, giving a complete untrusted-source-to-severe-sink path (inherent: critical). The only control on this path is a single behavioral prompt instruction, which rubric step 4 credits for one tier, giving residual: high. That instruction is classified dependent and is listed in control_decay.md as failing under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, and autonomy_increase; the runtime notes confirm the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so removing that one credit returns the finding to its inherent critical tier (forecast: critical). A second, property-level finding captures the absence of attributable logging for CRM reads and of any rate, spend, or step limit across both tool calls (high, uncredited by any declared control, capped at high per rubric 5a).

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the provided runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No agent card, tool JSON schemas, or orchestration/runtime config were provided beyond the runtime notes; approval-gate presence, definitions_pinned status, and peer_identity_verified status for crm_mcp and mail_mcp are inferred as absent, and confidence is medium to low where noted.

Whether inbound email authenticity (SPF/DKIM/DMARC or ticketing-system identity binding) is verified before processing is not stated in the artifacts; this materially affects the real-world likelihood of the cross-customer disclosure finding.
